headline: High-risk filesystem and shell overlap: xonsh can read/write and execute broadly, while the paired content-writing agent can emit untrusted instructions that may be consumed as data.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A can produce content that B may read from the shared workspace or stdin/stdout, and B explicitly parses shell commands and Python expressions with filesystem access. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than proven; uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF agent_a output is copied into files or stdin that agent_b consumes as instructions, injection becomes actionable.
IF the pair is connected through a shared workspace or pipe, B may treat A-authored text as executable content.
mitigations: Separate A and B into different workspaces.
Require a human review step before B executes any A-produced text.
Prefix A outputs as inert data, not commands.
Disable automatic ingestion of A outputs into B.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B can read filesystem contents and environment variables, and A has broad network egress. If A's outputs or shared files contain sensitive material, B can expose them indirectly through its network-capable workflows. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this remains inferred but plausible.
conditions: IF agent_a writes sensitive content into a location agent_b reads, B can incorporate it into network-bound outputs.
IF both agents operate on the same filesystem, leakage risk increases materially.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory.
Run B with a read-only mount where possible.
Block outbound network access for B during review runs.
Review A outputs before they are stored on disk.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has broad network egress and B has broad network egress plus filesystem write and shell execution. Even without documented shared state, overlapping write-adjacent capabilities can conflict over the same files or external resources if orchestrated together. The lack of explicit locking or shared-resource details means uncertainty escalates to medium.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or remote resource, writes may race or overwrite each other.
IF the orchestrator does not serialize access, shell-driven side effects can conflict.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Serialize access with a simple lock file.
Avoid concurrent runs against the same remote endpoint.
Use dry-run mode for B when possible.
requires-engineering: add resource arbitration in the orchestrator.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a content-writing agent, so its outputs can become inputs for B's shell-oriented workflows. B can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, so if it treats A's text as authoritative, errors can cascade into actions. No verification step is documented, so the safer medium rating is warranted.
conditions: IF B executes commands derived from A without validation, incorrect instructions can propagate into actions.
IF A produces malformed code or commands, B may run them as-is.
mitigations: Require B to validate commands before execution.
Insert a checksum or approval gate for A outputs.
Limit B to read-only analysis mode.
Log and review all A-to-B handoffs.
requires-engineering: implement schema validation for handoff artifacts.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, and both profiles are open-source docs-only. The only concrete compliance-relevant fact is B's filesystem and environment-variable access; without a stated regulated data class, the pairwise compliance risk is limited and not proven.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into B's filesystem or environment, compliance review is required.
IF deployment policy requires residency or retention guarantees, those must be checked before use.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in B's environment.
Confirm retention settings before deployment.
Document data classes allowed for the pair.
Restrict logs to non-sensitive content.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets.
